newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:

* U.S. Senate leaders said they will not hold confirmation hearings for Anthony Lake, President Clinton's nominee to be director of the Central Intelligence Agency, unless the Federal Bureau of Investgation provides all its files on Lake.

* The Pentagon said nearly all classified documents recording incidents of chemical weapons use during the Persian Gulf war remain missing despite an exhaustive search, raising veteran concerns about a cover-up or criminal incompetence.

* The Internal Revenue Service on Thursday banned a popular corporate investment on Wall Street, effectively halting billions of dollars of transactions that companies had hoped to use to borrow money at very low cost.
* Deaths from AIDS fell 13 percent in the first half of 1996, marking the first substantial decline in AIDS deaths since the epidemic of the disease began in 1981.

* The chairman for the Clinton-Gore campaign organized a White House coffee last summer specifically meant to solicit more cash from 10 wealthy Texas residents who had already contributed several hundred thousand dollars to the Democrats.
* The Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra agreed to admit a female harpist, ending a 155-year-old ban against women players.
* International organizations have begun silently retreating from Bosnia and Herzegovina, despite continued ethnic tensions between the region's Serbs, Croats and Muslims.
* New York City Chancellor Rudy Crew is proposing to change the city's school programs for gifted children in an effort to admit minority and immigrant students who he believes are being excluded.
